checklists.title: Lost your job in Australia? Start here
checklists.summary: Start with deadlines and the next fortnight's essentials. You can work through the rest with help.
checklists.scope: For employees in Australia. Federal workplace rules below apply to the national system; many state public-sector and council roles, and some WA employers, use state systems. Payment eligibility and claim options depend on your circumstances.

steps.title: Check the dismissal deadline today
steps.text: If you may challenge the dismissal, contact the Fair Work Commission, your union or a legal service now. National unfair-dismissal applications generally have a 21-day deadline after dismissal takes effect. Eligibility conditions apply; ask about other claims too, rather than ruling yourself out.

sources.title: Fair Work Ombudsman — Unfair dismissal
Fair Work Ombudsman — Which workplace system applies

steps.title: Keep your own employment records
steps.text: Save your contract, payslips, rosters, dismissal letter and a dated account of what happened. Keep records you can lawfully retain somewhere you control. Ask for missing employment records; keep employer-confidential files out of your personal archive.

sources.title: Fair Work Ombudsman — Record-keeping and pay slips

steps.title: Ask for an itemised final-pay calculation
steps.text: Check wages owing and any accrued annual leave. Ask whether notice pay, redundancy pay or long service leave applies; these are not universal entitlements. Confirm the payment deadline under your award, agreement and applicable law instead of assuming one final-pay deadline covers everyone.

sources.title: Fair Work Ombudsman — Final pay

steps.title: Check income support and possible waiting periods
steps.text: Check which payment fits your age and circumstances. JobSeeker has income, assets and residence rules; waiting periods can apply, including after leave or redundancy payouts. Gather requested evidence and keep claim references. Budget around confirmed money, not an unconfirmed approval or payment date.

sources.title: Services Australia — JobSeeker Payment
Services Australia — When you will get your first JobSeeker Payment

steps.title: Write a two-week essentials plan
steps.text: List available cash, confirmed income, rent or mortgage, food, medicines, utilities and necessary transport. Mark the next due dates. Identify the first shortfall so you can ask for specific help before making new commitments.

steps.title: Ask for hardship help before bills pile up
steps.text: Contact providers about affordable payment arrangements and keep written records. For free, confidential financial counselling, call the National Debt Helpline on 1800 007 007. Bring urgent notices and the essentials plan; tell the counsellor which payment is due first.

sources.title: Moneysmart — Financial counselling

steps.title: Choose the next work step before buying training
steps.text: Update one useful CV example, contact a reference or compare a few suitable roles. If retraining would help, check your state's Free TAFE options first: courses, eligibility and places are limited. Confirm materials, placement and living costs before enrolling.

sources.title: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations — Free TAFE

checklists.closing: If you only do one thing today, check any dismissal deadline. These are starting steps, not an assessment of your legal claim or payment eligibility. Open the current official source before acting.

checklists.title: Renting your first place? Read this before you sign
checklists.summary: Use this checklist at the inspection and before paying or signing. Save the move-in steps for when you collect the keys.
checklists.scope: For people renting in Australia. Tenancy rules are state and territory based; boarding, rooming, student accommodation and other arrangements may use different rules. The NSW example below is labelled and is not a national deadline.

steps.title: Find the rules for this address and arrangement
steps.text: Find your state or territory tenancy authority. Check which rules cover your accommodation type.

sources.title: myGov — Signing a rental lease and links for every state and territory

steps.title: Add the costs beyond the advertised rent
steps.text: Write two totals: the cash needed to move in, and the ongoing cost of living there. Include bond, permitted advance rent, moving, utilities, internet and transport. Check whether your budget still works after a quieter work week or an unexpected bill.

steps.title: Inspect the home and verify who you are dealing with
steps.text: Inspect the home. Independently verify the provider before sending money or identity documents.

sources.title: myGov — Checks before signing a rental lease

steps.title: Read the agreement before committing
steps.text: Check the names, address, rent, start date, lease length, payment method and extra conditions. Ask what happens if you need to leave early, and have unclear terms checked by a local tenancy service. Keep the agreement and any written repair promises.

sources.title: Moneysmart — Understanding rental leases

steps.title: Check how your bond will be handled
steps.text: For NSW, check Rental Bonds Online and keep your payment record. Elsewhere, use the authority you found in step 1. Agree and record each housemate's contribution.

sources.title: NSW Government — Rental Bonds Online for tenants (NSW only)

steps.title: Put the housemate arrangement in writing
steps.text: Agree on rent, bills, bond contributions and what happens when someone leaves. Check whose names are on the lease and obtain local advice about each person's responsibilities. A household spreadsheet or private promise does not by itself change the rental agreement.

sources.title: NSW Government — Sharing a rental property (NSW example)

steps.title: Plan the move-in evidence now
steps.text: Photograph existing damage before unpacking, complete the condition report and keep a copy plus proof of return. Check your local deadline: in NSW, the tenant returns a completed copy within seven days of moving in. Use your own jurisdiction's rule elsewhere.

sources.title: NSW Government — Rental property condition reports (NSW only)

steps.title: Ask how the property gets its electricity
steps.text: Ask whether electricity is supplied through an embedded network, who bills you and what tariffs and fees apply. Check your actual ability to choose another retailer before relying on a comparison quote. Add the confirmed arrangement to your housing budget.

sources.title: Australian Energy Regulator — Embedded network customers

checklists.closing: Keep the lease, receipts, photos and correspondence together. Before signing an unclear term or paying an unfamiliar charge, check the current rule with your state or territory tenancy authority or advice service.

checklists.title: Before your baby arrives: the Australian admin checklist
checklists.summary: Eight practical jobs to organise leave, payments and care costs now, and prepare the paperwork you will finish after birth.
checklists.scope: For households expecting a baby in Australia. Payment eligibility, workplace entitlements and insurance cover depend on your circumstances; registration processes differ by state and territory. This checklist focuses on administration, costs and timing.

steps.title: Get the full maternity-care quote
steps.text: Ask the maternity service about booking, referrals and out-of-pocket costs for appointments, tests, birth and follow-up. If using private cover, confirm waiting periods, exclusions and how and when to add your newborn. Save the answers before committing to a care pathway.

sources.title: Better Health Channel: Paying for pregnancy, birth and newborn care

steps.title: Put workplace leave dates in the calendar
steps.text: Check employer-funded pay and eligibility for unpaid parental leave separately. Under national Fair Work rules, eligible employees generally give 10 weeks’ written notice; continuous leave dates must be confirmed at least four weeks before starting. If the required notice is impossible, notify the employer as soon as possible.

sources.title: Fair Work Ombudsman: Applying for parental leave

steps.title: Check Parental Leave Pay before planning around it
steps.text: Check the work, income, residence and caring rules, including each parent's eligibility and any sharing rules. You can submit a claim up to three months before the expected birth. Set up Centrelink through myGov, gather the required details and remember that payment cannot start before birth and proof is required.

sources.title: Services Australia: Who can get Parental Leave Pay
Services Australia: How to claim Parental Leave Pay

steps.title: Make a budget for the leave period
steps.text: Map confirmed take-home income against housing, bills, baby essentials and care costs. Keep unapproved payments separate from money you can rely on, and check whether other family payments may apply. Agree who pays shared bills and which purchases can wait.

sources.title: Moneysmart: Having a baby

steps.title: Compare childcare places and the actual gap fee
steps.text: Ask services about vacancies, waitlists, session fees and your estimated bill after Child Care Subsidy. The 3 Day Guarantee applies to CCS-eligible families; it guarantees subsidised hours, not a place or free care. Plan the CCS claim before care starts, and confirm the provider's enrolment details through Centrelink.

sources.title: Department of Education: 3 Day Guarantee
Services Australia: Who can get Child Care Subsidy
Services Australia: How to claim Child Care Subsidy

steps.title: Prepare Medicare access; enrol your baby after birth
steps.text: Check your Medicare eligibility and online access now. If still on your parents' card, transfer to your own before enrolling your baby. After birth, use the signed Newborn Child Declaration as proof and enrol through the applicable family-payment claim or Medicare process. Babies born overseas, adopted or born through surrogacy have separate instructions.

sources.title: Services Australia: Enrolling your baby in Medicare

steps.title: Save the two separate after-birth tasks
steps.text: Bookmark your state or territory birth-registration process: registration is free, while a certificate may cost extra. Separately, finish any pre-birth Centrelink claim with the baby's details and proof of birth. For a pre-birth Parental Leave Pay claim, Services Australia says to provide these within 56 days of the child entering your care.

sources.title: Services Australia: Register the birth of your baby
Services Australia: Parental Leave Pay claiming timeframes

steps.title: Assign the practical jobs, with a backup
steps.text: Agree who will manage bills, paperwork, meals, transport and any older children's pickups during the first weeks. Keep deadlines and confirmations in one shared plan, and check that helpers have the necessary collection permissions. Share only the information they need; keep passwords private.

checklists.closing: Start with the next deadline, then work through the rest at your own pace. Keep claim receipts and written confirmations; revisit the plan if the birth date, leave or care arrangements change.
